newsitem.title: USA: Amgen Phase 3 SCF trials are positive.
newsitem.headline: Amgen Phase 3 SCF trials are positive.

text.p: Amgen said Phase three clinical trials showed positive results for its Stem Cell Factor when tested in breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
Amgen said it plans to file for Food and Drug Administration approval of SCF in the next few months.

SCF in a combined dose with Amgen's white blood cell stimulating factor, Neupogen, was shown to reduce the number of blood cell collection procedures required to help cancer patients overcome potentially toxic doses of chemotherapy.

Amgen said patients given the combination of the two drugs required a median of two fewer blood collection procedures to collect the optimum number of progenitor, or bone marrow stem cells. It said both groups of patients tested showed rapid blood cell recovery when the progenitor cells were reinjected.

Progenitor cells, which are the body's original cells that replicate to form other blood cells, are collected prior to chemotherapy and reinjected afterwards to help patients avoid serious side effects.
Amgen said facilitating blood cell recovery is critical in minimizing the period during which patients are at risk for serious side effects of chemotherapy.
